Version: Version determines the binary layout of EnvironmentHeader. It is not an artistic setting: the parser uses it to decide which offsets to read all subsequent fields from and where to find the string table.
SunDirection: Normalized world-space vector pointing toward the direct sunlight source. It determines which sides of the terrain and models receive direct light, as well as the opposite direction in which cast shadows fall.
SunColor: HDR RGB of the direct sunlight component. The color is applied primarily to surfaces whose normals face SunDirection, and sets the color tint of the world's lit side.
SunIntensity: Scalar multiplier of the direct sunlight. It changes the contrast between the lit and shadowed sides, without replacing the color or determining the light direction.
ShadowColor: RGBA of the shadow/ambient component used on unlit areas and inside cast shadows. The field changes not the shadow's geometry but its color and residual brightness.
WaterEnabled: The main CPU flag for the water render path. When disabled, the engine should not submit a visible water surface, even if the other water parameters and texture paths are filled in.
WaterDiffuse1Movement: Vector of the first diffuse/foam water projection: XY set the UV scroll over time, Z sets the texture repeat rate. This is one of two overlapping layers of the surface pattern.
WaterDiffuse2Movement: Vector of the second diffuse/foam water projection. Its independent direction, speed, and repeat rate break up the first layer's noticeable periodicity.
WaterNormal1Movement: Scroll and repeat parameters of the first water normal-map projection. This layer changes the orientation of small highlights and local refraction, not the base color.
WaterNormal2Movement: Parameters of the second water normal-map projection. Combined with the other normal layers, it forms multi-scale ripples.
WaterNormal3Movement: Parameters of the third water normal-map projection, typically adding a different scale or direction of choppiness.
WaterNormal4Movement: Parameters of the fourth water normal-map projection. This is the last independent scrolling normal layer in the shader layout as reverse-engineered.
WaterColor: Base RGBA tint of the water before reflection, refraction, specular highlights, and depth modulation. RGB sets the overall hue of the water body; alpha's contribution should only be judged within the full water blend path.
WaterRefractionScale: Scale of the underwater image displacement produced by the water normal field. The larger the magnitude, the more strongly the bottom and submerged objects appear to bend through the surface.
WaterReflectionScale: Scale of the water's reflective component. It controls the contribution or amplitude of the reflected environment/scene relative to the diffuse and refraction parts.
WaterFresnelBias: Base reflection fraction in the Fresnel blend. It shifts the entire transition between a top-down view and a grazing angle, while preserving its shape.
WaterFresnelPower: Exponent of the Fresnel curve. Determines how sharply the reflection strengthens as the view transitions from top-down to nearly parallel to the surface.
WaterDepthScale: Scale of the normalized depth's influence on water shading. Controls how quickly the transition goes from shallow water to visually deep water.
WaterChromaticScale: Strength of the color channel divergence in the water's refracted/reflected component. Larger values make colored RGB fringing more noticeable on high-contrast underwater detail.
WaterSpecPower: Exponent of the water's specular highlight. A large value narrows and sharpens the highlight; a small value spreads it over a wider area.
WaterBloomFactor: Multiplier of the bright water contribution fed into a glow/bloom-like result. The field affects the halo around the brightest highlights, if the corresponding post-process is active.
WaterWhiteCapCutoff: Threshold for extracting bright crests, or white caps, from the water signal. Lowering the threshold includes more of the surface; raising it leaves only the strongest areas.
WaterWhiteCapBrightness: Brightness of the areas that passed the white-cap cutoff. Changes the intensity of the already-selected crests, but not the threshold at which they appear.
WaterWaveTiming: Time coefficient of the procedural wave modulation. It affects the phase progression or speed of the large-scale animation, separate from the independent UV-scrolling texture layers.
WaterWaveModulus: Spatial modulus of the large-scale wave function. It changes the periodicity and the distance between repeating large wave features.
WaterFoamHeightOffset: Height offset of the condition under which foam appears, relative to the water/shore reference. It moves the foam band higher or lower on the shoreline geometry.
WaterWaveStartDepth: Depth threshold beyond which the given wave/deep-water behavior is applied. Separates shallow-water behavior from deeper water.
WaterDepthOriginXZ: World-space XZ origin of the depth-field rectangle. Together with the bounds size, it defines the transform from world coordinates into the depth map's UV.
WaterDepthBoundsSizeXZ: XZ size of the area covered by the water depth field. A scale error stretches or compresses the depth transition relative to the map's geometry.
MaxWaterDepth: Maximum world-space depth used to normalize the depth signal. The value determines the actual depth at which shading reaches the deep-water state.
WaterElevation: Main world-space elevation of the visible water plane. This is the surface's vertical position, relative to which shoreline, depth, and object submersion are evaluated.
WaterRenderElevationOverride: Additional elevation that the render/reflection path uses instead of WaterElevation when the value is positive. A negative value acts as a sentinel and leaves the main WaterElevation in effect.
WaterAuxParameter0: A raw float that gets copied into water-related runtime state, but no distinct shader consumer has been found yet. Its purpose cannot be reliably described as a visual setting.
WaterAuxParameter1: The second raw float of the same unidentified water runtime pair. Its routing and vanilla values are known, but its ultimate effect has not been proven.
AirElevation: Height reference plane from the original MapInfo. The field's name is confirmed by the source TDF, but no distinct, isolated visual consumer has been identified in the render branches examined.
ReservedZero236: Reserved float slot that is zero across all 56 PC maps examined. It is part of the layout, not an available artistic setting.
EnvironmentMap: Virtual path to the environment/reflection resource used by water/environment shading for the reflected surroundings. The vanilla resource may live outside the map's own archive.
SkyMap: Virtual path to the sky texture/resource. Replacing it changes the look of the distant background/sky wherever the map and camera allow it to be seen.
ReservedTexturePath: This string slot is empty across the whole PC corpus. An unknown non-empty path should be preserved, but must not automatically be treated as a known texture role.
ColorCorrectionCube: 3D LUT for the normal viewport, transforming the scene's final colors after the main lighting pass. Can change the contrast, channel balance, saturation, and tone of the whole world image.
FogOfWarCorrectionCube: A separate 3D LUT for the image under Fog of War. Lets the invisible/darkened area be visually distinguished from the normally-observed scene.
CoreFogColor: RGBA of the first fog endpoint, tied to the near/core part of the interpolation. The CPU blends it with HorizonFogColor, so it is not an independent single-color layer.
HorizonFogColor: RGBA of the far/horizon fog endpoint. At large distances its contribution grows and determines what the terrain visually dissolves into at the horizon.
CoreFogAmounts: Three density/blend coefficients of the core fog endpoint. They feed into the CPU's preparation of the final FogAmounts and change the fog's strength in the corresponding part of the transition.
HorizonFogAmounts: Three coefficients of the far fog endpoint. Control the fog's intensity toward the horizon after interpolating with the core set.
CoreFogDistances: Start and end distances of the core fog transition. They move the range over which the near fog begins and finishes gaining contribution.
HorizonFogDistances: Start and end distances of the horizon fog transition. Determine the depth range over which distant terrain transitions to HorizonFogColor.
PointCloudOrigin: Minimum world-space corner of the point-cloud volume, reconstructed from the source center minus half its size. Together with PointCloudSize it defines the effect's sampling volume.
PointCloudSize: Size of the point-cloud volume along XYZ. The runtime computes the reciprocal scale to convert world position into the volume's local coordinates.
GlowEnabled: CPU flag for the separable glow chain. When enabled, bright data passes through blur and is then blended with the original image.
GlowBlurKernelScale0: Scale of the glow chain's first blur kernel/direction. Changes the blur radius along one axis or pass.
GlowBlurKernelScale1: Scale of the second blur kernel/direction. Together with the first, it determines the two-dimensional size and shape of the glow halo.
PostProcessSourceWeight: Weight of the original, unblurred frame in the final post-process composite. This is not PointCloudLightAmount: the parameter controls how much of the original scene is preserved relative to the added glow result.
GlowBlurPassCount: Number of repetitions of the separable glow blur. A higher count widens and smooths the halo, while also increasing the GPU cost.
GlowBlurFactor0: Operational sample/composite factor of the glow blur's first direction. Affects the energy distribution and shape of the blurred result.
GlowBlurFactor1: The paired factor of the glow blur's second direction. Its effect should be judged together with KernelScale and the pass count.
BloomEnabled: CPU flag for the bright-pass and radial bloom chain. A controlled-delta test confirmed that enabling it activates BloomValues, the separable blur, and the radial passes.
BloomThreshold: Brightness threshold of the bright-pass. Pixels below the threshold should not produce bloom, while brighter ones become sources of the halo.
BloomDirectionCount: Number of directions/rays in the radial bloom sampling. Increasing it makes the pattern more even or adds rays, but raises the cost.
BloomDirectionPhase: Angular phase offset of the set of radial directions. Rotates the ray pattern around the bright source without changing the source's own position.
BloomSpreadDivisor: Divisor of the radial samples' spatial spread. Changes how far the bloom spreads from a bright pixel; zero is not allowed.
BloomSampleScaleX: Horizontal scale of the bloom sampling. Changing it in isolation stretches or compresses the halo along the screen's X axis.
BloomSampleScaleY: Vertical scale of the bloom sampling. Changing it in isolation stretches or compresses the halo along the screen's Y axis.
BloomResultWeight: Weight of the finished bloom result in the final composite. Changes the halo's brightness after it has been formed, without changing the threshold or the sampling geometry.
BloomPassCount: Number of radial bloom iterations. Additional passes can make the halo longer/denser and increase the GPU cost.
PointCloudLightAmount: Multiplier of the point-cloud effect's light contribution. Unlike position/size, it changes the strength of the result within the volume, not its placement.
FogOfWarLowerHeight: Lower world-space bound of the Fog of War height transition. Below it, the lower side of the resulting visibility curve is used.
FogOfWarHighestHeight: Upper world-space bound of the FoW height transition. Above it, the height coefficient reaches the opposite limit.
FogOfWarHeightStrength: Width/strength of the FoW height transition, also entering the calculation as 1/strength. A small value makes the boundary sharp and needs protection against zero.
IntelLowerHeight: Lower bound of a separate intel-visibility height transition. This is not RangeCircles: the field feeds the IntelHeightValues shader constant.
IntelHighestHeight: Upper bound of the intel height transition. Together with the lower bound and the strength, it defines how the intel visualization covers objects of different heights.
IntelHeightStrength: Strength of the IntelHeightValues transition. Controls how soft the height boundary is and enters a reciprocal calculation.
DepthOfFieldEnabled: Flag for the depth-of-field branch. When enabled, the frame's depth is used to separate the sharp range from the areas that get blurred.
DepthOfFieldStart: Near bound of the DoF depth interval. Moving it changes the distance at which the sharpness transition starts to appear.
DepthOfFieldEnd: Far bound of the DoF transition. Together with Start, it sets the width and direction of the blur's range of change.
SharpenStart: Starting depth distance of the sharpen-amount interpolation. Before it, the near-side sharpness value is used.
SharpenEnd: Ending depth distance of the sharpen interpolation. After it, the far-side value is used.
SharpenBaseAmount: Base sharpen amount to which the near/far offsets are added. Raises or lowers sharpness across the whole range.
SharpenNearOffset: Sharpen correction for the near side of the depth range. Applied together with the base amount to close-up detail.
SharpenFarOffset: Sharpen correction for the far side of the depth range. The shader interpolates by depth between the near and far values.
RenderPassACEnabled: Operational bool that enables a CWldTerrainRes branch through vtable slot 0xAC. The code builds a height-dependent auxiliary render-item pass; the exact object category has not yet been established.
RenderPassB0Enabled: Operational bool for auxiliary geometry batch/group paths through slot 0xB0. The exact layer name is missing from the stripped EXE.
RenderPassB4Enabled: Operational bool for a dedicated world mesh/resource pass through slot 0xB4. A visual test on SC2_MP_106 showed that disabling it removes a large lighting/environment contribution from the world, without darkening the HUD.
ShadowCastDistance: CPU distance limit for shadow-caster participation. The field determines how far from the camera or shadow setup geometric shadows continue to be submitted.
WindDirectionX: X component of the horizontal wind vector used by vegetation/unit shader animation. It should be considered together with Z and speed.
WindDirectionZ: Z component of the horizontal wind vector. Changes the direction of the leaf/vegetation pattern's movement in the map plane.
WindSpeed: Speed of the shader-driven wind animation. The field is layout-conditional: offset 504 is a float only if it lies before the header's first string.
